questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the verb qù frequently followed by?
Where does yǐqián come in Chinese, and where does "before" come in English?
What does yíge mean when stressed?
What does yíge mean when unstressed or toneless?
Write the Chinese for "Before I go to see the movie, I am first going to visit a friend."
Which other verb behaves like qù in taking a purpose phrase?
At which end of the clause does yǐqián stand?

answers.answer_text: At the end of the clause.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Where must the adverb xiān be placed?

answers.answer_text: Between the subject and the verb.

articles.text:
10. A: Qù kàn diànyǐng yǐqián, wǒ    Before I go to see the movie, I am
       xiān qù kàn yíge péngyou.      first going to visit a friend.

Notes on No. 10

Qù kàn: The verb qù, like the verb lái, is frequently followed by a phrase expressing the purpose of the action.

Yǐqián, "before": Notice that in Chinese yǐqián comes at the end of the clause, while in English "before" comes at the beginning.

Qù kàn diànyǐng  |  yǐqián
(Before          |  I go to see the movie)

Yíge: When the word yíge is stressed, it means "one." When the word is unstressed or toneless, it means "a" or "an."
